builder_plan.scenario: A workflow needs specialist review, but extra agents may add more cost than useful work.
builder_plan.change: Test the proposed division of work against a single-agent implementation.
builder_plan.baseline: One agent with the same tools and an equal total token and time budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted outputs, coordination failures, wall-clock time, and total cost across all agents.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: MULTILOOP: Evolving Multi-Agent Harnesses for Complex Information-Seeking Tasks
summary: Replaces hand-tuned multi-agent prompts and orchestration logic with a coding-agent loop that analyzes execution traces and edits the harness automatically. Costs iterative LLM calls for trace analysis and code editing, plus evaluation runs, and adds a meta-optimization layer of complexity over an already multi-component system. Orchestration failures specific to multi-agent systems, such as poor delegation and information sharing, largely persist after optimization, so gains may be limited to per-agent behavior fixes rather than structural coordination improvements.
rationale: The method runs on API-accessible models with tiny training data and shows real accuracy gains, making it feasible to pilot, but the persistence of orchestration failures means the reader must validate whether gains transfer to their own multi-agent workload before production adoption.

claims.statement: Replaces hand-tuned multi-agent prompts and orchestration logic with a coding-agent loop that analyzes execution traces and edits the harness automatically. Costs iterative LLM calls for trace analysis and code editing, plus evaluation runs, and adds a meta-optimization layer of complexity over an already multi-component system. Orchestration failures specific to multi-agent systems, such as poor delegation and information sharing, largely persist after optimization, so gains may be limited to per-agent behavior fixes rather than structural coordination improvements.
With only 10 training samples, the evolved harness improves accuracy by 4.6% over the base harness and by 3.2% over the best single-agent system on DeepSearchQA.
